headline: The US 10 year Treasury yield hit a 19 year high of 5.2251 percent on 24 September and still ended the week near 5.184 percent, yet all three US indices posted weekly gains as Meta added 12.9 percent on its Muse AI agent and easing oil took WTI down 7.84 percent on the week.

summary.us: The S&P 500 closed 25 September up 0.51 percent at 7,743.41, the Nasdaq Composite up 0.48 percent at 27,068.72 and the Dow up 0.93 percent at 51,828.62, snapping a three week losing streak, as reports of a phased US and Iran arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz pulled WTI down 2.29 percent to 92.44 dollars. The 10 year Treasury yield ended at 5.184 percent after reaching 5.2251 percent on 24 September, its highest since June 2007, on stronger than expected manufacturing surveys, hawkish Fed commentary and a poorly bid five year auction, while University of Michigan sentiment fell to a four month low on fuel prices and tariffs; Microsoft rose 3.66 percent on its revamped Copilot, Qualcomm 3.97 percent as buyers reversed the Apple royalty renewal selloff, and Meta gave back 3.33 percent after a 12.9 percent week.
summary.india: Nifty 50 closed 0.34 percent higher at 23,140.50 and the Sensex 0.43 percent higher at 73,895.74, with Bank Nifty up 0.26 percent at 55,580.40 and Nifty IT down 0.17 percent, as auto and realty names led a partial recovery from the previous session's IRDAI driven selloff and moderating crude helped sentiment. The rupee gained 19 paise to 95.80 per dollar on softer crude and reported RBI intervention, India VIX fell 4.18 percent to 12.16, and the insurance distribution consultation paper kept pressure on platform names with PB Fintech down another 3.41 percent for a 33.1 percent weekly loss and Paytm down 3.54 percent, while Axis Bank rose 3.03 percent and Bajaj Finance 1.52 percent ahead of the 5 to 7 October MPC meeting.
summary.global: The Nikkei 225 rose 1.30 percent to 66,364.20 for a fifth straight gain as Japanese bank stocks jumped on a 30 year high in the 10 year JGB yield and expectations of further tightening after the Bank of Japan took its policy rate to 1.25 percent, with Mitsubishi UFJ's ADR up 4.03 percent; the Hang Seng fell 1.01 percent to 24,510.09 in a third straight decline, and mainland China, Korea and Taiwan were shut for holidays. Europe closed higher with the DAX up 0.56 percent at 25,408.64 on easing oil and the US-China trade truce extension to 10 January 2027, led by Adidas, Commerzbank and Deutsche Bank, while the dollar index eased 0.25 percent to 101.04 from a two month high and gold held 4,320.50 dollars with silver up 1.97 percent to 64.71 dollars.

weekly.narrative: The bond market set the terms all week: the US 10 year Treasury yield reached 5.2251 percent on 24 September, its highest since June 2007, and the 30 year touched 5.47 percent, a 22 year high, on strong manufacturing surveys, hawkish Fed commentary and a poorly bid five year auction, which pushed the dollar index to a two month high. Equities absorbed it anyway, because a reported phased US and Iran arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz took WTI down 7.84 percent on the week and because Meta's Muse AI agent kept re-rating the largest index weights, lifting Meta 12.9 percent over five sessions while knocking bank stocks on 23 September as investors weighed whether agents could shop deposit rates on a customer's behalf. India went the other way, undone by a domestic regulator rather than by yields, after the IRDAI consultation paper on insurance distribution economics proposed commission caps and a five year glide path on expenses of management, taking PB Fintech down 33.1 percent on the week and dragging Nifty 50 to a 0.88 percent weekly loss even after Friday's rebound. Precious metals broke their run, with gold off 2.36 percent and silver off 2.77 percent on the week as real yields and the dollar bit, though both recovered on Friday, and copper held a 2.48 percent weekly gain near its 22 September record; crypto diverged from that risk-off tone, with bitcoin adding 3.38 percent and capital rotating into compute and DeFi tokens even after the Bitget hack. Next week the macro calendar is a labour market week rather than an inflation one, with JOLTS on 30 September, ADP and ISM manufacturing on 1 October and jobless claims and factory orders on 2 October, before the RBI Monetary Policy Committee meets 5 to 7 October with the repo rate at 5.25 percent after four pauses.
